fact: 1914年8月4日，英国以德国入侵比利时、破坏比利时中立为由对德宣战，宣战于当日23时生效。8月4日下议院在数分钟内通过5.25亿美元（约1.05亿英镑）的紧急拨款及数项法案，乔治五世同日宣布陆军动员。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Austria-Hungary: The outbreak of war
sources.quote: In the night of August 3–4 German forces invaded Belgium. Thereupon, Great Britain, which had no concern with Serbia and no express obligation to fight either for Russia or for France but was expressly committed to defend Belgium, on August 4 declared war against Germany.

sources.title: Harrisburg Telegraph, 1914-08-04（Chronicling America 影像 OCR）
sources.quote: LONDON, AUG. 4.—THE HOUSE OF COMMONS TO-DAY VOTED $525,000,000 FOR EMERGENCY PURPOSES AND PASSED SEVERAL BILLS IN FIVE MINUTES WITHOUT A DISSENTING VOICE. Great Britain sent a virtual ultimatum to Germany demanding a reply by midnight on the subject of Belgium neutrality. King George proclaimed to-day the mobilization of the British army

fact: 1914年8月7日，陆军大臣基钦纳呼吁再招募10万人，组建「新军」；8月4日至9月12日陆军部共接收47.89万名新兵，其中8月30日之后的13天内就有30.1971万人入伍，到10月初约75万人报名。英国在1914年没有义务兵役制，扩军完全依靠自愿。

sources.title: Imperial War Museums, First World War Galleries 导览手册
sources.quote: Kitchener's first appeal on 7 August 1914 was for ‘an addition of 100,000 men’ to the Army. Within eight weeks nearly 750,000 men had enlisted. They pledged to serve as long as the war lasted.

sources.title: University Officers' Training Corps and the First World War（Occasional Paper No. 4）
sources.quote: Those who remained with the OTCs heard the call of the new secretary of state for war, Earl Kitchener of Khartoum, on 7 August for the first 100,000 men ... Between 4 August and 12 September, the War Office accepted 478,893 recruits, with 301,971 attested during the 13 days from 30 August onwards

fact: 1914年8月8日《国防法》（Defence of the Realm Act, 4 & 5 Geo. 5 c. 29）获御准：国王会同枢密院可在战争期间发布规章，授权军事法庭审判并处罚违反规章者，处罚方式如同其受军法约束、在现役中犯《陆军法》第5条之罪。该法成为新闻审查、禁止传播「可能引起军民不满或惊慌之报道」、征用建筑与土地的法律基础。

sources.title: legislation.gov.uk, Defence of the Realm Act 1914（King's Printer 原始文本）
sources.quote: An Act to confer on His Majesty in Council power to make Regulations during the present War for the Defence of the Realm. [8th August 1914.] ... His Majesty in Council has power during the continuance of the present war to issue regulations ... and may, by such regulations, authorise the trial by courts martial and punishment of persons contravening any of the provisions of such regulations designed—(a) to prevent persons communicating with the enemy or obtaining information for that purpose ... in like manner as if such persons were subject to military law and had on active service committed an offence under section five of the Army Act.

fact: 1914年8月5日，英国在一个下午内通过《外国人限制法》（Aliens Restriction Act）：16岁以上外国人须向警察登记，内政大臣可将其驱逐出境，并首次引入签证制度。到9月9日，已有近6.7万名德国、奥地利与匈牙利籍人士登记；敌侨离住处超过5英里须申请许可，不得持有通讯器材、摄影设备、军事地图与机动车，东南沿海及若干国防要地被划为禁区。

sources.title: GOV.UK, The Historical Roots of the Windrush Scandal: independent research report
sources.quote: it took just one afternoon on the 5th August 1914 to push a new piece of emergency legislation through Parliament. ... The new Act required aliens over the age of 16 to register with the police, and they faced new restrictions on their activities, as well as being liable to be deported if the Home Secretary thought it conducive to the public good. ... and introduced visas for the first time.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Internment in the United Kingdom during the First World War
sources.quote: Under the Aliens Restriction Act, passed on 5 August, all foreign nationals were required to register with the police, and by 9 September just under 67,000 German, Austrian and Hungarian nationals had done so. ... Enemy aliens were also required to obtain a permit to travel more than five miles from home, and they were prohibited from possessing means of communication ... and owning photographic equipment, military maps and motorised transport.

fact: 1914年7月30日至8月1日，英格兰银行把银行利率从3%提高到4%，再提高到8%，最后提高到10%，为当时世界最高；7月31日（星期五），伦敦证券交易所自成立117年来第一次在营业日关门，此前一周外汇与货币市场已先崩溃。

sources.title: Richard Roberts, The Great Financial Crisis of 1914（LBMA Alchemist, Issue 73）
sources.quote: it raised the bank rate from 3% to 4% and then to 8%. ... The political authorities’ condition, based on past precedent, was a 10% bank rate. This was duly implemented – the highest rate in the world. ... Then on Friday 31 July, the London Stock Exchange, for the first time in its 117-year history, shut its doors.

fact: 伦敦证券交易所在1914年7月31日至9月14日关闭；9月14日仅恢复部分龙头股的现货交易，并设定最低限价；10月31日政府宣布由英格兰银行在政府担保下垫付同业贷款，金额约8000万英镑；1915年1月4日才恢复一般业务，全部为现货并设大量最低价。1915年1月18日起资本发行受财政部管制。

sources.title: Bank of England Archive, History of the Bank of England 1939-1945, Part IV, Chapter VII（述1914年证券交易所）
sources.quote: In 1914 the Stock Exchange was closed from the 31st July to the 14th September. On the latter date dealings in certain leading stocks were resumed for cash, with fixed minimum prices; and on the 31st October the Government announced a scheme under which the Bank of England would make advances under a government guarantee in respect of account-to-account loans, the amount of which was then about £80 million. The Exchange re-opened for general business on 4th January 1915, when all dealings were for cash and many minimum prices were fixed. ... Capital issues were controlled by the Treasury as from the 18th January.

fact: 1914年8月，英国发行由财政部印制、面额1英镑与10先令的「布拉德伯里纸币」（Bradburys），以替代金币流通，并实行全面延期支付（general moratorium）；该延期原定一个月，两次延长后于11月4日解除。8月19日招标发行1500万英镑国库券，到年底未偿额约1亿英镑，1919年达12亿英镑。

sources.title: Richard Roberts, The Great Financial Crisis of 1914（LBMA Alchemist, Issue 73）
sources.quote: The principal crisis containment measures, devised and introduced during the long bank holiday, were the issuance of Treasury currency notes and a ‘general moratorium’. The Treasury notes were small denomination notes that were paper substitutes for the sovereign [£1] and half sovereign [50p] gold coins. ... It was eventually lifted, without incident, on 4 November. ... On 19 August, there was an auction of £15 million of Treasury bills. By the end of the year, there was £100 million outstanding and, in 1919, there was £1.2 billion outstanding.

fact: 1914年11月，在证券交易所仍关闭期间，英国发行第一笔战争公债（War Loan），总额3.5亿英镑，劳合·乔治称之为世界史上最大规模募资；实际认购仅2.37亿英镑，缺口1.13亿英镑，为掩盖失败，英格兰银行首席出纳与其副手以秘密提供的资金个人认购了缺口部分。

sources.title: Richard Roberts, The Great Financial Crisis of 1914（LBMA Alchemist, Issue 73）
sources.quote: November 1914, while the Stock Exchange was still closed, saw the first War Loan bond issue. At £350 million, it was, Lloyd George proudly told the House of Commons, the world’s biggest ever fund-raising. However, due to various miscalculations, the issue was a fiasco ... only £237 million of the loan was subscribed for, leaving a shortfall of £113 million ... the Bank of England’s Chief Cashier and his deputy personally subscribed for the missing millions

fact: 1914年7月1日，英国4磅重面包（quartern loaf）零售价在4.5便士至7便士之间，按销量加权全国平均5.5便士；伦敦1914年1月的平均零售价同为5.5便士。作为对照，同期伦敦一磅肉约1先令1便士、一磅黄油1先令6便士、一夸脱牛奶5便士、一磅糖4便士。

sources.title: Hansard, HC Deb 01 August 1918 vol 109 cc625-6W（Bread，引贸易委员会统计）
sources.quote: The Board of Trade returns show that on 1st July, 1914, the price of the 4 lb. loaf varied from 4½d. to 7d., and having regard to the larger quantity sold at the lower figure, it was estimated that the average price for the whole Kingdom was 5½d. per quartern loaf.

sources.title: Hansard, HC Deb 27 February 1929（Wheat and Bread Prices，伦敦1914年1月零售价）
sources.quote: The average retail price of the 4-1b. loaf in London, as compiled by the Ministry of Labour, was 5½d. in January, 1914, and 8¼d. in January, 1929.

sources.title: The Great World War: A History, Vol. IV（London, 1916）每周家庭食品预算表
sources.quote: Meat (12 lb., average, 1s. 1d. per pound) ... Butter (2½ lb., at 1s. 6d. per pound) ... Milk (10 quarts, at 5d. per quart) ... Sugar (3 lb., at 4d. per pound)

fact: 1914年8月4日，英国议会批准国家战争险方案：在伦敦设国营保险局承保货物战争险，政府对船壳战争险再保险80%，船东协会自留20%；国家收取的保费为统一费率，上限每百单位5几尼、下限1几尼。开战时市场战争险费率高达每百单位50至70几尼，方案实施后单程船壳费率定为1.25%，9月初降为1%。

sources.title: Hansard, HC Deb 04 August 1914（War Risks）
sources.quote: it is proposed that the work should be undertaken by a State Insurance Office to be opened in London. It has already been opened. ... The rate of premium to be charged by the State for covering these risks is to be a flat one, irrespective of the voyage or the character of the cargo ... within a maximum of five guineas per cent. and a minimum of one guinea per cent.

sources.title: Preliminary Economic Studies of the War: The Financial History of Great Britain, 1914-1918（Carnegie Endowment, 1918）
sources.quote: The rates for war insurance vary from 60 to 70 guineas per hundred for vessels belonging to any of the four continental Powers ... the government took over the insurance of vessels then on voyage to the extent of 80 per cent, the associations carrying the other 20 per cent. ... At first the rate was fixed at 1¼ per cent on hulls for single voyages and 2½ per cent on round voyages.
